hypotheses.text: Autoinflammatory or interferonopathy-associated cutaneous manifestations (such as chilblains) occur in less than 10% of PSMD12-related STISS individuals across published series.
hypotheses.rationale: STISS has recently been linked to proteasome-mediated autoinflammation and type I interferon dysregulation, but clinical signs like chilblains appear restricted to rare individuals rather than forming a classic penetrant feature.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 24 additional unrelated patients with STISS, chilblains resembling signs observed in interferonopathy were noted in only 2 individuals, despite cellular induction of type I interferon-stimulated genes.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: Of note, 2 patients also showed chilblains resembling signs observed in interferonopathy.

evidence.text: In a family cohort of six individuals with truncating PSMD12 variants, none presented clinical manifestations of autoinflammation and IFN-I signature perturbations were non-specific.

source.title: Does It Run in Your Family? Inherited Truncating PSMD12 Variants Broaden the Phenotypic Spectrum of Stankiewicz‐Isidor Syndrome
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: None presented clinical manifestations of autoinflammation and the detected IFN-I signature perturbations were not specific.

hypotheses.text: Isolated congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (specifically horseshoe kidney) represent a rare presentation of PSMD12 variants, accounting for under 5% of isolated fetal horseshoe kidney cases.
hypotheses.rationale: While CAKUT is part of the syndromic presentation of STISS, it is important to delineate the frequency with which PSMD12 mutations manifest as prenatally detected isolated renal malformations without upfront syndromic dysmorphism.

evidence.text: Among 45 fetuses with isolated horseshoe kidney who tested negative by CMA and underwent trio exome sequencing, one case of disease-causing PSMD12 variant (c.796-1G > A) was identified.

source.title: Clinically Significant Genetic Results in Fetuses With Isolated Horseshoe Kidney
source.quote: Notably, two disease-causing variants, c.796-1G > A in PSMD12 and c.11707 C > T (p.Gln3903*) in KMT2D, were detected in each case.

hypotheses.text: Preaxial upper limb anomalies constitute a recurrent diagnostic hallmark present in at least 15-25% of individuals with PSMD12 loss-of-function variants across expanded cohorts.
hypotheses.rationale: Digital and skeletal anomalies are common in STISS, but characterization of specific preaxial involvement (such as thumb hypoplasia, duplication, or preaxial polydactyly/brachydactyly) provides high discriminating value against other syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders.

evidence.text: Analysis of 24 additional unrelated patients confirmed preaxial hand abnormalities as an expanding core feature of STISS.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: In addition to previously reported DD/ID, speech delay, cardiac and renal anomalies, we also confirmed preaxial hand abnormalities as a feature of this syndrome.

evidence.text: A familial cohort described skeletal anomalies across all 6 individuals, along with novel digital/ectodermal anomalies like unilateral ectopic fingernail (onychoheterotopia).

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerators and denominators for congenital heart defects (stratified by VSD, ASD, PDA) across the combined Küry 2017 and Isidor 2022 patient cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Congenital heart disease is reported as a recurrent feature, but exact subtype breakdowns and cumulative prevalence across the combined ~48+ patients will define its specificity.

new_directions.question_text: Does the expressivity and severity of craniofacial and limb anomalies differ between familial inherited PSMD12 variants and de novo mutations?
new_directions.rationale: Familial transmission was reported by Feresin et al. 2025 with intra- and inter-familial variability; comparing frequencies between inherited and de novo cases can establish if hypomorphic or mosaic alleles cause milder presentations.
